text:
maya: Heads-up — customer Acadia opened an escalation. After we onboarded Cerulean v1.2 their p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~420ms to ~2.1s on long inputs (>12k tokens). They started seeing 504s and client retries. Happened after model/tokenizer cutover at ~2025-12-03T10:00Z.
jon: Any request ids or sample payloads? link to the dashboard would help (p95/p99 panels).
maya: Posted a request id in the support ticket: req_34c9a1f2. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/acadia/overview — p99 panel shows correlation with sequence length.
ops-bot: Alert: CERULEAN_LONGCTX_P99 threshold breached (10:12 UTC) — affected cluster: hosted-us-west-2.
eli: Quick triage: I repro'd locally with a ~14k token doc and see a tokenizer slow-path call that spikes CPU and causes synchronous normalization. On profiler I see long serial work in the tokenization stage (unicode normalization + fallback merges). Notably we hit a CJK-heavy fallback in this customer's inputs.
tara: Could be the new tokenizer normalization rules in v1.2. We changed the merge heuristics to avoid over-splitting which can cause extra passes on multibyte runs.
jon: Can we get the exact stack sample? Also does KV cache behavior change for very long prefixes (we recently tweaked kv partitioning)?
eli: Stack sample (trimmed):
```
Tokenize::normalize_unicode()
Tokenize::split_long_runs()
Tokenize::apply_merge_heuristic()
ModelServe::prepare_kv_cache()
ModelServe::generate()
```
I also captured a timeline: tokenizer took ~850ms of the 1.8s p99. Rest was kernel scheduling/IO waits.
maya: Customer logs show 504s at our edge and then retries piling up; they’re seeing client-side backoff. This is on hosted and one dedicated pool they use.
jon: Repro steps for infra/devs: curl to our hosted endpoint with long payload and header X-Request-ID=req_34c9a1f2. Example: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/models/cerulean-v1.2/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_34c9a1f2" \
  -d '{"prompt":"'$(python -c 'print(\"longword \"*3000)')'","max_tokens":1024}'
```
eli: Also tried a trimmed repro with repeated CJK block and it regresses faster.
tara: Short mitigation options: 1) rollback tokenizer changes (v1.1) for Cerulean (quick), 2) pin Acadia to cerulean-v1.1 until we patch, 3) add a server-side fast-path that bypasses the expensive normalization for long inputs with high multibyte ratio.
jon: Ops action: Can we push a routing rule to pin traffic from Acadia to cerulean-v1.1? Support-bot, can you request a customer pin?
support-bot: Raised pin request ticket #SUP-8812 to ent-ops, marked P2.
maya: I'll ask Acadia to accept the pin temporarily.
eli: For longer-term fix I can add an early heuristic to detect long multibyte runs and use simplified normalization (saves ~600ms in my tests). I'll open PR today and add unit tests + regression harness.
tara: If we release the heuristic, we should also add a canary and monitor tokenization CPU and error rate.
jon: Temporary mitigation we can deploy in 15-30m: a per-customer model-route override to v1.1 and apply short TTL so other customers unaffected. Ops, please prepare.
ops-bot: Runbook step executed: created route override entry for Acadia -> cerulean-v1.1 (ttl 1h) by jon.
maya: Customer confirmed acceptance of temporary pin, their error rate dropped overnight in their dev tests.
eli: Follow-ups: PR #4892 (tokenizer heuristic), regression harness entry, add sample inputs from Acadia to our corpus, and schedule a dedicated performance run on the dedicated pools.
tara: Also add a notice to the onboarding checklist: when changing merge heuristics, include a 10k+ token CJK-heavy test.
jon: I'll own rollout gating and canary metrics. tagging @eli and @tara as owners for fix + postmortem.
maya: Thanks team — keeping this thread updated as things change. :thumbsup:
